readout_other: Morris water maze; Y-maze; novel object recognition; hippocampal LFP; Abeta immunofluorescence; western blot; RNA-seq
direction_notes: TUS pulsed at 40 Hz improved memory, reduced Abeta and neuroinflammation and raised hippocampal gamma power in 5xFAD mice; no excitation/inhibition polarity assessed.
safety_notes: Skull temperature rise 1 to 2 C; H&E and Nissl staining showed no hemorrhage or neuronal damage.

exposures.label: TUS to bilateral hippocampus and cortex (TUS1-TUS4 groups)

timing.protocol_description: 0.5 MHz, PRF 40 Hz, 1.25 ms tone burst, 1 s sonication, 10 s interstimulus interval; 20 min twice daily for 7 or 14 d.

exposures.label: BV2 microglial cells, ultrasound from beneath culture plate

timing.protocol_description: In vitro: ultrasound applied from beneath the culture plate for 10 min; the remaining parameters same as in vivo (0.5 MHz, PRF 40 Hz, 1.25 ms tone burst, 1 s sonication, 10 s interstimulus interval).

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The parameters for ultrasound delivery were as follows: 0.5-MHz center frequency, 40-Hz PRF,

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: 1.25-ms tone burst duration, 1-s sonication duration, and 10 s interstimulus interval. TUS was performed twice daily for 20 min. In the parameter study, the spatial-peak temporal-average intensity $( I _ { \mathrm { s p t a } } ; 0 . 3 3$ or 2.14 W/cm<sup>2</sup>) and total treatment duration (7 or 14 d) were varied, including TUS1 (0.33 W/cm for 7 d), TUS2 (2.14 W/cm<sup>2</sup> for $7 \mathrm { d } )$ , TUS3 (0.33 W/cm<sup>2</sup> for 14 d), and TUS4 (2.14 W/cm<sup>2</sup> for 14 d), while other parameters were kept the same. For sham treatment, the ultrasound transducer was placed on the head of mice; however, no ultrasound wave was emitted. The $I _ { \mathrm { s p t a } }$ and total treatment duration were determined based on a previous study [ 22 , 23 , 53 ]. The selected $I _ { \mathrm { s p t a } }$ parameter corresponded to an $I _ { \mathrm { s p p a } }$ of 42.6 W/cm<sup>2</sup>, which is well below the Food and Drug Administration 190 W/cm<sup>2</sup> limit for diagnostic ultrasound [ 22 ].
